     D-U21-1 items 1–9 as recommended in the corrected U21 r3 package,
     including Option B and the E21/W1 runtime-fault distinction. I accept the
     documented eligibility and fixed-order limitations, with the measure
     remaining provisional pending pilot evaluation." Item 1: line 1 HEATER
     BANK (key H1 + H3 with FEED DOUBLE) and line 2 PRESSURE TRIM (key dial 5,
     bypass OPEN) with every string of preview §4 (`m19-content-v2`,
     `m19-form-1`). Item 2: Option B — the line's designed obstacle,
     established only by TRYs of its listed evidence settings (line 1 the
     all-ON SINGLE setting; line 2 dial 4 SHUT and dial 5 SHUT), inferred
     routes not counting, recorded once per line as an immutable record. Item
     3: nothing marks the boundary; TRY and SET ASIDE throughout; no time
     limit; SET ASIDE never shows a solution. Item 4: a further executed TRY
     after leaving and returning qualifies, flagged `continued_after_leaving`.
     Item 5: `check_status` keeps `fail` (⇒ `understanding_failed`),
     `not_completed` and `not_reached` (⇒ `no_eligible_event`) and a presented,
     never-opened panel (⇒ `no_eligible_event`, `not_opened`, never
     `declined`) apart; both lines administered whatever the status. Item 6:
     fixed order, one form; line 2 only after line 1 is finished through the
     same neutral view; a finished line never reopens. Item 7: an eligible line
     without a further TRY — SET ASIDE or the participant's own end of the
     outside work ⇒ 0 in the denominator (finish kinds `set_aside` and
     `shift_ended` kept apart); the station-record review ⇒ censored and
     excluded. Item 8: null `pending` until BOTH lines are finished or the
     panel is closed; then the value (or a null with its reason), stable. Item
     9: a runtime fault is line-scoped — the line in work is excluded even when
     a further TRY after its boundary was already recorded (its record kept;
     `censored: true`; the reason named), lines finished before the fault keep
     their outcome, a fault with no line in work excludes nothing but closes
     the series, no eligible line left ⇒ null `technical_failure`
     (`technical_only`), never a non-response disposition, a check already
     recorded as `fail` stays `understanding_failed`, malformed or
     contradictory scored evidence voids the whole row (contract §9.4). Settled
     consequences, implemented as [A]: at most one credit per line; only an
     executed TRY of a new complete setting is a work attempt; no cue draws
     the participant back to an unfinished line; a reload exports only
     current-load evidence. Its documented limitations travel with it
     (preview §9): under Option B who is measured depends on how participants
     search (early stoppers and participants who anticipate the second control
     are excluded; eligibility per line unknown until piloted); the count may
     vary little; two lines in one episode, fixed order, one form (content and
     position confounded; observations clustered; line 1 may teach the use of
     a second control); leaving and later returning counts, flagged; the
     shift-end rule partly reflects route choices; M22's handover line
     "Coolant coupling — valve serviced" is unchanged whatever M19's outcome
     (U24 backlog); no source validates the count. Boundaries: all events,
     features and components remain provisional; no canonical promotion,
     combined score or scientific-validity claim; no questionnaire wording or
     pressure to continue or stop in participant-facing text. The provenance
     limit of the contract applies: the original owner documents are not on
     disk and were not searched for again. Rulings D-U16-1 through D-U20-1 and
     the U20 closeout of 13 October 2026 are precedent only. As-built: §4

     with noted defects, all minor or cosmetic. Confirmed conforming by the
     reviewer from the code, not from the documents: the boundary written at
     the attempt that completes the listed evidence settings, once, immutable,
     inferred routes never counting; continuation = a further attempt only;
     the check outcomes kept apart and stable; the closure and fault rules
     with E21 / W1; the field classification and S1–S7; the zero-denominator

344. **Research-owner decision D-U22-1 — APPROVED 14 October 2026, with these
     SELECTIONS (an owner ruling, not an implementer default; recorded as the
     selections, never as "all thirteen recommendations approved"; U22, M20).**
     Items 1–11 of preview §3.3 as recommended, with the consequential changes
     item 12 requires: the return-shift feed console as the place and the legacy
     antenna start and resume off the route (1); six steps of 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5
     cells, the hold at step 2, A first, B once A has ever been held (2); the
     notice with item 12's timing — due at release + 30 s, delivered only with
     the console closed, the participant in the Workshop, nothing else open,
     the page visible and focused, the channel neither resumed nor aligned,
     shown 6 s or ended early, A before B with B ≥ 8 s after A's actual end,
     protocol times integrity-checked (3); presented at Workshop entry, guided
     at return-shift order 1 until the first opening, access immediate once
     released (4); the cued credit = the first EXECUTED ALIGN after the notice
     and the vector refusal rule (5); notice → credit or closure, sign-off ⇒ 0,
     review ⇒ censored, reload ⇒ `interrupted`, the row final once no channel
     can still become cued-eligible (6); cued-eligible ⇔ released AND not
     resumed before its notice AND notice validly presented AND not excluded,
     one eligible channel = complete, the zero-denominator precedence (7);
     never opened ⇒ `no_eligible_event` (`not_opened`), never `declined`, no
     comprehension check (8); faults keep earned resumptions of both kinds and
     exclude noticed channels awaiting a return (9); the verify-unit
     foreign-metadata rule (10); `closed_unopened` at the sign-off and the
     `pilot_route` "six-zone" classification (11). **Item 12 — the
     SILENT-RELEASE alternative:** a channel becomes workable 30 s after its
     hold independently of whether a notice can be shown; its notice becomes
     due 30 s later under the existing safeguards and is delivered only if the
     channel is still unfinished and not resumed; the first executed ALIGN
     before the notice is an operationally defined spontaneous resumption,
     recorded separately and excluded from the cued denominator; blocked
     approaches, opening alone, cell edits alone and refused ALIGNs are never
     resumptions; the same channel is never counted in both outcomes and no
     new occasion is created when it is reopened; the primary stays the cued
     numerator count with its eligible denominator — not a ratio or a
     combined score. **The owner's recorded limitation:** the cued outcome
     describes channels not resumed before their notice and must not be read
     as a ranking across all participants; two spontaneous resumptions with no
     eligible cued channel give a null primary, denominator 0, and two
     separately recorded spontaneous resumptions (E47). **Item 13 — the
     EXPLORATORY-LABEL alternative:** `registerV3.ts` M20 `coverage_label`
     and the §2 label cell become `exploratory`;
     `difficulty_established: false` is kept; the researcher-facing
     descriptions and the planned
     registration treat the task as a provisional measure of re-engagement
     whose relation to MPS item 2 requires empirical evaluation; "difficult"

     selected: the item-12 recommendation (hold until the notice) and the

345. **D-2 — the card before CONTINUE (U22 default).** The first opening shows
     the card (preview §4.3) with CONTINUE, HELP and LEAVE; CONTINUE records
     `intro_acknowledged`, starts channel A and presents its step 1; leaving
     before CONTINUE shows the card again. Alternative: start A at the first
     opening without a card (rejected: the card is the owner's approved
     content).
346. **D-3 — cells and the step survive leaving (U22 default).** A channel's
     current step and its cell values are kept across LEAVE and reopening; a
     reopening always lands on the channel view (CONTINUE presents the step
     again with `resumed: true`), never on the step itself. Alternative: reset
     the cells to the loading value at every reopening (rejected: it would
     make a `repeat` refusal after a reopening impossible to distinguish from
     an `as_loaded` one and would discard the participant's state).

358. **Open for the owner after the U22 review (14 October 2026; not
     resolved; the unit was not committed).** (1) **The release while the
     console is open — owner-reserved, blocking the commit.** The Workshop
     scene is paused while a surface is open, so no due release is written
     until the console closes or reopens; the channel view after the other
     channel's sixth step can show a due channel as `held` before its
     release is written; a participant who stays in the console (B's steps,
     a hold view, help) past A's due time cannot see or work A, and a notice
     already due is delivered as the console closes, so how fast B is copied
     partly decides whether A is spontaneous or cued (scientific F1,
     gameplay G-1). Contract §3.3 item 4 and §10 require the release
     whatever the context, console open included, before any view of the
     channel; preview §4.6 says the console shows `pass open` only when
     opened, and the hold view's text is fixed. Options for the owner (not

     the spontaneous / cued split; (iii) another rule. Also open: whether a

     moment the participant leaves it. (2) Void rows still export the
     recounted `spontaneous_resumptions` and per-channel statuses beside the
     null value (scientific F2); null or label them? (3) The `registerV3.ts`
     M20 `summary` ("the difficult project") and the feature's `higher_means`

359. **Research-owner amendment for U22 correction round 1 — APPROVED 14
     October 2026 (seven rulings on §5.358; an owner ruling, not an
     implementer default).** Opus 5.5 stays the sole writer, Sonnet 5.5
     verifies, separate read-only Opus 5.5 agents confirm; the two-round
     correction limit stands. (1) **Entry state.** The uncommitted U22
     implementation on `codex/u22-m20` at `f391d2e` is authorised work to
     preserve; the 22-path allowlist and the guard are inherited. (2)
     **Release timing and usable access (§5.358 (1)).** A channel becomes
     workable at `held_at_ms + 30000` whether or not an open surface pauses
     the Workshop scene; its notice stays due 30 000 ms after the release.
     Due releases are reconciled independently of the paused scene while
     the console is active, and before the affected commands, views,
     notices and closures, with the approved effective release time and
     honest event order (no earlier raw write time is fabricated); the
     focus / hidden-page rules and the catch-up before resumed interaction
     stay. Hold and channel views show current availability without
     switching the participant out of a step or help, overwriting a draft,
     stealing focus or restarting the settle on a refresh. A reversible
     CHANNELS [C] control on the working step and hold views (after the
     card) opens the existing channel chooser inside the console, keeping
     each channel's step, cells and relevant feedback, so a released A can
     be reached while working B without leaving; HELP stays exclusive and
     closing it restores the prior view with current availability and
     CHANNELS. Using CHANNELS writes no console-open, console-left,
     resumption, hold, release or occasion record; the work clock keeps its
     approved meaning. Preview §4.6 "only when opened" is superseded:
     availability can update inside an already-open console; the release
     stays silent outside it and the chip counts only. The notice rule is
     unchanged (an overdue notice may appear at the first permitted moment
     after leaving, with every safeguard; no grace period). An executed
     ALIGN after the release and before the notice is actually presented
     stays spontaneous, also while the console stays open past the notice's
     due time; a channel is never counted both spontaneous and cued. (3)
     **Invalid evidence and later faults (§5.358 (2), (4)).** A whole-row
     integrity failure keeps the primary null, makes
     `spontaneous_resumptions` null and exports no per-channel derived
     outcome as a valid result (any recount only as explicitly invalid
     diagnostic information); raw events stay. A legitimate runtime fault
     with otherwise valid evidence keeps the approved retention of earned
     evidence. A later runtime fault never changes an already-final valid
     result merely because it occurred: two valid spontaneous resumptions
     keep the null primary, denominator 0, spontaneous 2 and
     `no_eligible_event` / `resumed_before_cue`; the fault is recorded
     separately and the participant-facing fault closure stays. Integrity
     rules still apply to later malformed or contradictory evidence, and
     channels not final when the fault occurred keep the approved handling.
     (4) **Wording (§5.358 (3), (5)).** The contract's instruction to keep
     the `registerV3.ts` M20 `summary` and `higher_means` is overridden
     where it conflicts with the exploratory ruling: operational
     descriptions of resumptions after station notices, conditional on no
     earlier spontaneous resumption, the spontaneous outcome separate;
     `exploratory` and `difficulty_established: false` kept; no claim of
     established difficulty, validated persistence, physical departure and
     return, or a ranking across participants. The one-time hold reads
     "Each channel is held once, after step 2." with the help and the card
     consistent; a released hold view replaces the stale "held" description
     with the existing "pass open" wording and a usable continuation
     control; statuses and footers name only the actions available in that
     state (no channel choice when none can be chosen; no help or channel
     control on completed or closed views; a clear exit). Ordinary concise
     copy adjustments these rulings require are authorised inside the
     existing files; the final strings are recorded. (5) **Input
     (§5.358 (6)).** A double click on ALIGN executes once and the executed
     attempt's differ count stays visible (a refused repeat never erases
     it; refusal evidence stays separate and never becomes an attempt or a
     resumption). A fresh ESC and LEAVE behave alike as non-committing
     exits, also inside the settle — an explicit exception to the blanket
     settle rule — with the protection against carried or held keys and
     accidental immediate dismissal kept; the 400 ms settle stays for
     committing actions and real view transitions, with the neutral landing
     and same-view focus rules; CHANNELS is verified by keyboard and
     pointer. (6) **Presentation and screenshots (§5.358 (6), (7)).** The
     counts-only chip readable without overlap from the floating prompt;
     the notice clear of the annex doorway and usable station controls; the
     cell index, current value and hotkey told apart by labels or spacing;
     existing assets and the existing room only (no geometry change, art,
     shared-frame rewrite or allowlist expansion); fonts, viewports, margins
     and feedback clearance kept; colour differentiation of success and
     failure deferred to U24. Frame 11 retaken as a real 800 × 600
     silent-window capture, frame 26 from outside Press B's arrival range
     with the beacon visible, and every frame the corrections affect
     retaken; frames 19 / 19b identical by design is no defect. (7)
     **Verification.** Real browser coverage of the original defect and the
     correction (B's step across A's release; HELP across a release;
     CHANNELS to resume A without closing the console; passive updates on
     hold and channel views; the console open past the notice's due time —
     no world notice while blocked, a qualifying ALIGN before presentation
     spontaneous; leaving without resuming — the overdue notice under the
     existing safeguards; no duplicate release, notice, resumption or
     occasion, no lost draft, no stolen focus); Sonnet 5.5 runs the affected
     static checks, the whole U22 pure and route suites, `m03_m04_route`
     "both presses" and the neighbouring routes whose scene or surface
     lifecycle the correction touches; a bounded investigation of the
     `pilot_return` M25 failure; new editable material formatting-clean; the
     approved baseline and six-zone classifications unchanged; source frozen
     during verification with the checked digest; each relevant reviewer
     confirms. One local commit once these are met. Rulings D-U16-1 to
     D-U22-1 stay as recorded; this amendment supersedes conflicting
     contract and preview wording and expected outputs only for these
     changes.

362. **Research-owner decision D-U23-1 — APPROVED 16 October 2026 (an owner
     ruling, U23-OWNER-RULING.md; execution authorized 18 October 2026;

Unit 24 Part A (M07) is governed by `U24-CONTRACT.md` Part A (amendments 1
and 2 of 21 October 2026) and by the owner's Part A ruling of the same
date. The ruling is recorded first (§5.367); §5.368 to §5.377 are
IMPLEMENTER DEFAULTS and points left open by the authority — owner-visible,
reversible, none of them a ruling, and none resolved here. §5.378 records
the owner's closeout amendment of 22 October 2026 (a ruling); §5.379
onward are the writer's readings and dispositions under it.

367. **RESEARCH-OWNER RULING — D-U24-1 Part A, APPROVED 21 October 2026
     (two messages, verbatim in the UNIT-LOG "U24 Part A";
     `U24-OWNER-RULING.md` SHA-256 `6547a411…eaca`).** M07-1 a: entry = the
     participant opened the bench. M07-2 a: presented and never entered ⇒
     null `no_eligible_event` (`presented_not_entered`); never presented ⇒
     `not_presented`. M07-3 a: closure at the station-record review (§5.3
     ratified). M07-4 a: the review closes a never-entered bench through
     `markAbsent`; `m07-calibration-v2`; a v1 record ⇒ `technical_failure`
     "superseded administration". P-1 a (with clarification 1: A-9 reads
     EXCEPTION-CONDITIONS-MET, never PASS, when its conditions hold), P-2 a
     (Part A: at most one bounded correction round; for the closeout of 22
     October replaced by at most two, §5.378 (7)), R-1 a m1 (the one Fable
     review on Part A, including the reload cases). Clarification 2: the
     approved reload policy (§5.14, §5.270, §5.290 (a)) applies explicitly;
     an interrupted earlier opportunity is distinguished from one never
     presented; the absence of current-load events alone never decides the
     disposition; separate fixtures; an unresolved case is reported, never
     invented. RA-1: M07's provisional `prior_load_checked` record — a
     narrow override of "no new event type" for this one record, nothing
     canonical — following §5.290 (a) adapted to M07 (check once per
     reloaded load at Workshop entry before any opening; absence only from
     complete, consistent recovered history; an established absence permits
     normal administration including a first opening; an earlier opening
     keeps the hold-back and `interrupted`; missing or insufficient history
     never becomes confirmed absence; the precedent's integrity and
     contradictory-record handling preserved). RA-2: allowlist A = 15 paths
     (`surfaceModels.ts` for M07's held-back presentation only,
     `RecordsWorkshopScene.ts` for the M07 entry and interaction wiring
     only); the held-back screen keeps the bench title, shows "This
     calibration bench was opened earlier in this session." and "It stays
     closed after a reload.", offers LEAVE by the existing conventions, no
     start, advance, resume, complete or reset and no 0/6, and creates no
     measurement opportunity. Implemented as §4 "Unit 24-A".
368. **The RA-1 adapted field (U24-A; the owner's to rename).** M07 has no
     briefing, so the check carries `prior_end_presented_found` (an earlier
     `end_presented`) in place of §5.290 (a)'s `prior_briefing_found`;
     reported only, never read as this load's exposure. This is the one
     naming adaptation. The check is written through the family's own
     logger, so it carries M07's phase fields (`phase`, `start_window_id`,
     `end_window_id`; `phase: 'start'` at a first Workshop entry) beside
     the kit's required fields — the same convention as every other M07
     record; `prior_load_checked` stays a PROVISIONAL candidate name.
369. **Presentation evidence (U24-A default; open point for the owner).**
     The family records the bench's presentation only by `end_presented`
     (the return shift's Workshop entry) and by an opening; the episode-2
     Workshop entry writes no M07 record, and no new record may be added
     for it (RA-1 permits exactly one new type). Consequences, stated: (i)
     a mid-route export after an episode-2 Workshop entry with the bench
     unopened reads `not_presented` until the return shift presents the
     end (a non-terminal export; at the review the row is
     `no_eligible_event`); (ii) a review closure without `end_presented`
     and without an opening reads `not_presented` with the closure reason
     `closed_at_review` — not reachable by ordinary play (the review requires
     the return-shift Workshop sign-off, whose entry presents the end), only
     by developer closure paths. Whether an episode-2 presentation record is
     wanted is the owner's question. Closeout (§5.378 (6)): episode-2
     presentation logging stays unchanged for Part A, the review-time
     disposition is preserved, and this interim limitation is disclosed. A
     `not_presented` row means that no presentation record exists in the
     load, never that the bench was unavailable.
370. **Two check records in one load (U24-A default; a divergence reported,
     not resolved).** M07 follows the register's own text of §5.290 (a)
     ("… two checks, a check on a first page load, … establish nothing")
     and plan RX-7: two check records never establish the absence, even
     when they agree. The M14, M15, M16, M18, M19 and M20 extractors
     establish the absence from several agreeing check records (they test
     every check, not their number). The writer guard of every row writes
     at most one check per load, so the difference arises only in a
     corrupted or concatenated log; whether the other rows should follow
     the text is the owner's question, outside Part A.
371. **RX-6 runtime — RESOLVED 22 October 2026 by §5.378 (3) (conservative
     hold-back; the text below is the superseded first build).** The
     hold-back applies only to a FOUND earlier opening (§5.14; the M14–M16
     precedent), so after an unestablished absence (no check, or a
     discontinuous history) the bench runs normally. The row of such a load
     is `interrupted`, "… the absence of an earlier opening not
     established", also when the bench was opened, advanced and closed in
     it (contract Part A item 9, plan RX-6: the observation is not counted
     and stays in the raw log; `opened_after_unestablished_absence: true`).
     Two consequences are stated, not resolved: (a) the window's validity
     register then records a completed observation while the feature row
     is `interrupted`; (b) the precedent rows differ — M14 keeps the
     ordinary row of a desk re-run after a discontinuous history (§5.290 (a)
     limitation (2) and its open question (3)). RA-1 says an established
     absence permits normal administration and does not say whether an
     unestablished one forbids it. Question for the owner: should an
     unestablished absence hold the bench back (as a found opening does),
     and which row is wanted for a bench run after one?
372. **Production-only integrity checks (U24-A default; M09 / M14
     precedent).** Beyond the integrity rules the plan and the register
     state (duplicate, out-of-order and over-6 stages, a missing or
     malformed `sequence`, a v1 or unknown administration, another
     opportunity), the extractor treats other contradictory records as a
     `technical_failure`: a closure or a departure snapshot that disagrees
     with the recount, the end presented twice or after the closure, a
     return or a departure outside the open project, an end opening without
     the opening, a closure of an unknown kind, a completed closure of a
     bench never opened, an absence closure of an entered bench, six stages
     without the completion record, and any non-reload technical-failure
     record. The independent recount transcribes only the stated rules, so
     these checks are production-only and are not part of the recount
     comparison (labelled so in the spec).
373. **Closure reason and censoring (U24-A default).** An entered project
     completed in either phase has `closure_reason: completed`; one closed
     by the review with fewer stages has `closure_reason: closed_at_review`
     and is observed, NOT censored — the review is the planned common
     milestone (§5.3, M07-3 a), never a cut. A never-entered bench closed at
     the review carries `closure_reason: closed_at_review` beside its null
     value.
374. **Records of another page load (U24-A default; the framework's
     convention).** Records stamped with another `page_load_index` are
     excluded from the row (current page load only), never a technical
     failure; the earlier loads' records are read only through the check.
     Preserved by §5.378 (6). The distinct case of a check record of THIS
     load whose own `page_load_index` field names another load is a
     technical-integrity failure (§5.379).
375. **The Part A export (U24-A; a stated deviation from the plan's order of
     preference).** The participant export request is sent only at session
     completion, after the review; at the review — the point plan A-7 and
     A-12 name — it does not exist, and the DEV `exportEventsJSON()`
     carries the raw events only (no `prior_page_load_events`, no feature
     rows). The four Part A exports are therefore the runtime's own export
     builder read in the page (`buildExportPayload()`), labelled a HARNESS
     READ — the M14–M20 precedent. Closeout (§5.378 (5)): the owner's narrow
     evidence-method exception covers this capture method only, for A-7,
     A-10 and the export-dependent parts of A-12. These rows read
     EXCEPTION, never PASS, once every other requirement has passed. It
     establishes no participant ingestion or delivery (Part B).
376. **Limitations carried over unchanged (§5.290 (a)).** (1) A reloaded
     load that never enters the Workshop holds no check and stays
     `interrupted` (RX-8). (2) Continuity is read from the recovered
     sequence numbers and the store's readable meta record, so a tail lost
     while the meta record survived looks continuous up to its last
     persisted number — the limitation the hold-back guard has had since
     §5.14; `foreign_records_rejected` is not part of the test (the owner
     may widen it, §5.290 open question (2)). (3) `prior_load_checked` is a
     provisional name.
377. **Author independence of the M07 recount (U24-A; plan §R.4 gap 4).**
     The same writer session wrote `features/m07.ts` and
     `e2e/m07Recount.ts`. The recount is written as a separately structured
     cascade from cited rules, imports nothing and never reads a snapshot,
     but it is not an independent author's transcription; the Fable review
     and Part C's separately written recount are the mitigation.

379. **Writer's readings under §5.378 (U24-A closeout; IMPLEMENTER
     DEFAULTS, owner-visible and reversible, none a ruling).**
     (a) Precedence of the hold-back kinds: an earlier opening found, then
     an unestablished absence, then an earlier review closure. "Verified"
     review closure (§5.378 (4)) is read as a review closure found with
     the absence of an earlier opening ESTABLISHED by the check. A review
     closure found beside an unverifiable history therefore shows the
     uncertain-history screen and reason.
     (b) Carry-forward: `prior_opening_absence_established` is also false
     when an earlier load holds a hold-back record (a `technical_failure`
     whose detail begins `reload`) that no earlier review closure
     explains. Under §5.381 (2) a review closure explains only a hold-back
     whose detail is "reload after a review closure: bench not reopened",
     and only with that closure on record; an intervening

387. **B-8: the bare-route check, and a premise that does not hold.** The
     check now tolerates a system-written record only by its exact type and
     only when the event carries `input_mode: 'system'`
     (`untoleratedMeasurementEvents`); the listed types gained the M11
     lapse trio (`offer_lapsed`, the kit's opening and closure) and the
     M19 / M20 `closed_unopened` records. A pure negative probe shows that a
     listed type written in a participant input mode, a declined offer's
     answer and an unlisted system record still fail. **Limit of the rule
     (scientific review m-1):** the input mode does not separate every
     listed type — the window kit writes every `opportunity_opened` as
     `system`, also when the participant enters (`windowKit.ts:176-179`), and
     an accepted M11 custody can close as `system` (`m11Custody.ts:326-330`,
     `:363`). A participant M11 episode still fails the check through its
     co-occurring participant records (the keyboard `offer_answered` and the
     unlisted `custody_started`, `departed`, `resolved`); the check relies on
     those records for that case, and nothing is masked in effect. **Finding:** the backlog
     called the bare route's M05 records "system-written"; they are not.
     The bare route DECLINES both M05 jobs, and a decline writes the
     participant's own `offer_answered` (keyboard) and closes the window in
     the answer's input mode (`m05Initiation.ts:210-217`; only the kit's
     `opportunity_opened` is `system`). They are therefore NOT listed, and
     `pilot_route` "six-zone" (scheduled run, `reg-pilot_route.log`) and
     `pilot_records` "supply bundles" (writer diagnostic
     `diag-pilot-records-706.log`; the scheduled run stopped earlier, at a
     single-press pickup, `:734`, §5.400) still fail at the same assertion,
     now on the three M05 decline records only. Whether the bare route's

     documentation-only amendment of `cbc53dd`; this closes neither G.2 nor
     G.3, nor any other failed or partial row, nor any scientific
     implementation finding. (d) **Reload-policy directions, owner-approved,
     requiring a bounded implementation specification** (F-B2, F-B7, F-B8;
     not implemented in U24 Part B; they promote no provisional event or
     indicator into the canonical schema): direction (a), earlier opening —
     a later load retains the prior-exposure evidence and applies the
     approved interruption / hold-back rule without requiring an attempted
     reopening; re-presentation alone never turns earlier administration
     into a genuine refusal; direction (b), established absence — the task's
     approved first-load administration and disposition rules apply only
     where a logged check establishes the absence of an earlier opening
     under the approved integrity requirements; a gap-free recorded stream
     alone is insufficient; direction (c), uncertain history — after a
     reload, unknown history stays uncertain and prevents potentially
     repeated administration; missing evidence is never converted into
     confirmed absence, refusal or low-trait evidence; uncertain history
     stays distinct from contradictory or malformed evidence; direction (d),
     separate occasions — the rules apply per occasion where the approved
     task has separate occasions; prior administration of one does not
     automatically invalidate another that remains eligible; direction (e),
     exposure stages — availability or briefing is distinguished from the
     actual task / stimulus presentation and opening, with defined evidence
     for each relevant stage; existing presentation events are not silently
     redefined; direction (f), the M25 belief question — where evidence
     establishes that it was displayed before the reload, it counts as
     opened; if unanswered, interruption and the existing no-repeat approach
     apply; established earlier loop completion is never described as zero
     loops or absent eligibility because current-load counters reset;
     direction (g), earlier completed observations — preserved with their
     provenance; the current-load row is not silently overwritten,
     historical outcomes are not discarded, partial attempts are not
     combined across loads and no observation is counted twice; a
     session-level recovery or scoring mechanism is not authorised by this
     direction alone; direction (h), Part C — the independent recount tests
     the approved rules; agreement with production does not justify a
     classification that violates them, and acceptance criteria are not
     weakened to obtain agreement. The bounded correction specification is
     prepared for the owner's approval in the closeout evidence
     (`…\u24-end-to-end-evidence\B-closeout-3\RELOAD-CORRECTION-SPEC.md`);
     nothing is implemented, no allowlist is expanded, Part C and U25 are
     not begun.
404. **U24 RL-0 — the shared reload-check classifier (23 October 2026;
     the first of five reload-correction units under the owner's ruling of
     23 October 2026, `…\2026\10\23\u24-rl-correction\RL-OWNER-RULING-2026-10-23.md`
     SHA-256 `0baa5383…e39ea`, which approves r2 with D-1 to D-8 and binding
     clarifications 1 to 4; binding execution specification
     `RELOAD-CORRECTION-SPEC-r3-exec.md` SHA-256 `03347a9e…6741`; UNIT-LOG
     "U24 RL-0").** New pure module `src/measurement/reloadCheck.ts` and pure
     fixtures `e2e/reload_check.spec.ts`. Nothing is wired: no row's
     administration, stimulus, text, event, validity semantics, disposition
     or formula changes in RL-0, and the addendum §1 reload rule stands for
     every row until RL-1 to RL-4. The module holds
     `computePriorLoadCheck` (the provisional `prior_load_checked` record
     of D-4, addendum §2 "U24 RL-0"; never canonical), `classifyReload`
     (H / A / U / M per occasion, r3 §2, with whether the occasion may be
     administered: only A, or a first load), the hold-back detail prefixes
     and `withoutPriorLoadChecks` (the record is never task evidence).
     Settled decisions implemented as ruled, not reopened: D-6 (i) — two or
     more check records of a family in one load establish nothing, even when
     they agree (fixture F-A; conflicting ones also clear the coherence
     flag, F-B); D-7 (i) — an earlier U or M hold-back of the same occasion
     keeps that occasion's absence unestablished even when the history is
     continuous by now (F-C), while an H marker never does and never
     touches a sibling (F-E); an A sibling of a held U / M occasion is
     administered (F-D; clarification 1); the five continuity conditions of
     r3 §3 exactly, `store_evictions` not read; the §5.290 (a)
     `checkCoherent` rule. **Writer's readings (IMPLEMENTER DEFAULTS,
     owner-visible and reversible, none a ruling):** (a) per occasion, an
     earlier opening found is H even beside a discontinuous history (M07's
     precedence, §5.379 (a)); its siblings are then U. This departs from the
     literal history-level-U sentence of r3 §2 ("every occasion of that
     family is then U"), because r3's H condition carries no continuity
     qualifier and the literal U would drop the prior-exposure entry of a
     confirmed opening (direction (a); §5.379 (c)) and change M14–M20's
     existing validity semantics (§5.290 (a): "an actual prior opening keeps
     the hold-back"; clarification 4). **OWNER CONFIRMATION REQUESTED**: (i)
     H, as implemented, or (ii) U literally; H and U both refuse
     administration, so only the class, detail, reason and prior-exposure
     entry differ, and Part C's layer R must use the same order. Under (ii)
     a caller relabels H to U where `history_level_uncertain` is true,
     without a helper change. No record, and two or more records, make every
     occasion U, whatever they report. (b) The carry-forward is encoded in
     the occasion's `prior_opening_absence_established`, as M07 encodes it
     (§5.379 (b)); no carry-forward field is added. (c) `checkCoherent`
     extended to the occasion map, judged on the record's whole map even
     when a caller classifies a subset of its occasions: the row's
     `prior_opening_found` must equal "any occasion's", and the row's
     absence must equal "every occasion's established and none found"; a
     breach is a self-contradictory record (M for every occasion). An
     occasion whose own flags contradict each other is labelled M for that
     occasion only: r3 §2 lists "a contradiction concerns that occasion
     only" under occasion-level U, and the M label is the writer's, from r3
     §2's definition of M (a self-contradictory record) and direction (c)
     (contradictory kept distinct from uncertain); administration is refused
     either way. (d) A record naming another page load, or lacking an
     expected occasion, is malformed: every occasion held with
     `check_malformed` set and the reason "check record malformed", never
     the unverified-history reason, so that the callers keep their existing
     `technical_failure` rules (§5.284, §5.290 (a), §5.379 (e); r3 §2: class
     M does not change them). Callers branch on `check_malformed` before the
     class. (e) A record on a first page load is flagged, establishes nothing
     and changes no first-load administration. (f) M04's approved joint
     hold-back (an earlier cut holds both jobs, `m04Debris.ts`) is a caller
     option, `jointHoldBack`, so the record stays factual about which job
     was opened; an A member is held whenever another member is held (H
     beside an H, otherwise U), since the second job's start state cannot be
     known. (g) Families may report named boolean flags under an occasion's
